title: ר' אלעזר בן פדת
author: Heilprin source tradition; Warsaw digital witness

paragraphs: Rabbi Elazar ben Pedat. (a) He is the unqualified Rabbi Elazar among amoraim: Rashi, end of Shabbat’s first chapter, 19, beginning of b; Yevamot 72b, 111b; Niddah 8a; Gittin 31b.

(b) Apparently a priest: Mo'ed Katan 28a, when the Angel of Death appeared, he said, “Am I not eating terumah?” His hour passed and he did not die then. This cannot be Rabbi Elazar ben Shammua the priest: all those death-angel stories concern amoraim—Rava, Rav Nachman, Chisda, Chiyya, Ashi. Heilprin cites Semag and David Abudarham for Rabbi Elazar leaving during the priestly blessing when weak. In the checked Yerushalmi Berakhot passage, however, the weakness is explicitly ascribed to Yehudah ben Pazi, who stands behind a pillar, and Elazar goes outside. Semag reads Shimon ben Pazi and Eliezer and explains both actions as ways of avoiding the summons when weak.

(c) Eruvin 54b, “Be always enraptured by its love”: he studied Torah in Sepphoris’s lower market while his sheet lay in the upper market. Yitzchak ben Elazar said someone once tried taking it and found a snake coiled on it. “They sent from there” means Rabbi Elazar, Sanhedrin 17b; see Yose bar Chanina. From Babylonia: Ketubbot 112a, on ascending to the Land, he said, “I escaped one,” a severe scriptural curse; ordained, “two”; admitted to the intercalation council, “three.” Apparently he ascended young, marrying in Tiberias; see below. Shekalim calls him “this Babylonian Rabbi Elazar”; Bamidbar Rabbah has the incident. Called master of the Land of Israel for expertise in blood. A woman brought blood while Rabbi Ammi sat with him. Rabbi Elazar declared desire-blood, pure. Rabbi Ammi questioned her: her husband was away and she desired him. He applied “The Lord’s secret is for those fearing Him,” Niddah 20b. See Berit Shalom, Tazria, why this earns the title. Chullin 44b: he accepted no gift from the nasi’s house and declined its meal invitations. Eruvin 54a: his student incurred heavenly burning; “Leave him: he served a great man.” Ein Yaakov reads Eliezer ben Yaakov; the Gemara’s unqualified R.A. might mean Eliezer the great or Shammua. Rabbah bar bar Chana: “When we followed Rabbi Elazar to visit the sick [לשיולי בתפיחא],” etc., Shabbat 12b. Hassefinah: “I saw those geese,” etc.; “When I came before Rabbi Elazar,” etc. Zaken Aharon, 131, identifies him as Shimon bar Yochai’s son, author of Zohar; Rabbi Elazar’s “They will be judged” means Israel neglecting hidden Torah, as Zohar often says. But mistaken: this is unqualified Rabbi Elazar ben Pedat, since Shimon’s son was much earlier than Rabbah bar bar Chana. Understand. Ta'anit 25a: extremely poor, shown thirteen balsam rivers in the world to come. Rashi: an amora.

(d) His learned son Pedat bore his father’s name; Rabbi Elazar instructed his son Pedat, see there. Tosafot, Niddah 8a, on “Pedat said”: Berakhot 5b suggests he had no sons. Perhaps one was born later, or many died, leaving this one. End of Heilprin’s quotation. The checked Tosafot says that some of his sons died and that Rabbi Yochanan spoke to comfort him. Berit Shalom, Tazria: “I think the bloodletting illness of Ta'anit 25a is Berakhot’s visit by Rabbi Yochanan, who saw him weeping: ‘If for sons, this is my tenth son’s bone’ (see Rabbi Yochanan). Then he had no son while ill; because he refused the world’s destruction and recreation under another fortune—livelihood and sons depend on fortune, not merit—this merit brought Pedat’s birth.” See there. He is bar Kappara’s sister’s son. See under pe, Bar Padda, for the source of Yuchasin’s error.

(e) Rabbi Yochanan’s student, Temurah 25b; Bava Batra 154b [Warsaw text gives chapter 13, 135b]: “If Rabbi Yochanan denies Rabbi Elazar his student.” Yevamot 96b likewise; Jerusalem Talmud, Shekalim, chapter 2, at מ״ב א׳ [locator retained]; Mo'ed Katan 3:7; Berakhot 2, mishnah 1. Rabbi Elazar reported without Rabbi Yochanan’s name; Rabbi Yochanan was offended. Rabbi Ammi and Rabbi Assi failed to appease him; Yaakov bar Idi succeeded: “Rabbi Elazar expounds unqualified, but all know it is from you, as Joshua from Moses.” Tosafot, Yoma 4a, takes one of Rabbi Elazar’s unattributed interpretations to be in Rabbi Yochanan’s name, citing this episode as precedent. Yoma 53, end of a: departing Rabbi Yochanan, he walked backward as from the Divine Presence. Bava Batra 7b: “Rabbi Elazar my son, fix nails in it”; Rashi: rule thus firmly. Yevamot 72b: Rabbi Yochanan to Resh Lakish, “Have you seen ben Pedat expounding like Moses from the Almighty?” Keritot 27a: Rabbi Elazar asked; Rabbi Yochanan: “How many years he has grown among us without hearing this law from me!” Berakhot 16a: the priests Rabbi Ammi and Rabbi Assi arranged his wedding (Jerusalem Talmud adds Chiyya); meanwhile he went to Rabbi Yochanan’s academy. Thus he married in Tiberias, Rabbi Yochanan’s place. Rabbi Yochanan spoke in his name, Shabbat 31b. Ein Doreshin 13a: “Come, I shall teach you the Chariot.” “I am not old enough.” After Rabbi Yochanan’s death, Rav Assi offered it: “Had I merited it, I would have learned from your teacher Rabbi Yochanan.” Difficult: Yevamot says Rabbi received his deserts when Yishmael told Avdan “your teacher,” not “Rabbi”; see there. Perhaps Rabbi Elazar was Rabbi Yochanan’s student-colleague, as Jerusalem Talmud, beginning of Sanhedrin: “A student-colleague, such as Rabbi Elazar toward Rabbi Yochanan.” Menachot 84b; Bekhorot 5a and 56a: “I saw Rabbi Yochanan in a dream; I shall say something excellent.” Rashi: knowing he would say something sound today because Rabbi Yochanan appeared last night.

Eruvin 66a: Shmuel’s house, his teacher; Bava Batra 82b: does Rabbi Elazar reject his teacher Shmuel? Chullin 111b: he stood before Shmuel when fish was brought to the table. Rav too was like his teacher, Kol Habbasar 111b; Bava Batra 135b, “from our master.” Rashbam identifies “our master” as Rav [Heilprin attributes the gloss to Rashi]. He asked Rav, Shabbat 153a; Eruvin 65b’s Eliezer is an error for Rabbi Elazar. Jerusalem Talmud, Ketubbot 9:5 and Kiddushin 1, end of halakhah 4: Chiyya’s student; in the Jerusalem Talmud’s Kirah chapter, Elazar quotes Oshaya saying, “I served Chiyya the great”; Terumot 4:1, in his name. Apparently Oshaya too taught him: Rabbi Elazar in Oshaya’s name, Shabbat 28b; Rosh Hashanah 4b, 14a; Berakhot 32b; Pesachim 103, end of b, 115a; Chagigah 17a; Mo'ed Katan 8b, 24b; Chullin 74b; Hoshaya’s name, Yoma 41a. Oshaya in Rabbi Elazar’s name, Pesachim 108a—perhaps the second Oshaya. Resh Lakish was offended at his failure to name him, Menachot 93b.

Kiddushin 33a–b, “a scholar is not permitted to stand,” etc.: the ruling follows Rabbi Elazar over Yannai, although Elazar was Yannai’s student’s student—Yannai taught Rabbi Yochanan, who taught Rabbi Elazar. See Responsa Sh.A. [ש״א; work unresolved], end of section 78, at רכ״ו ג׳ and דקי״ג ד׳ [locators retained]; Chavvot Yair; above, legal ruling, section 28.

(f) Abba; Abba bar Kahana in his name; Abba bar Zavda spoke to him; Abba b.bar Chana followed him (see there). Abbahu and Avin in his name. Rav Adda Karchinai challenges him. Oshaya in his name, and he in Oshaya’s (see above). Rav Acha in his name; Ilai; Inyai bar Sisi in his name. In Shammua’s name, Chullin 7a; Zevachim 65b; Azaryah’s name, Yevamot 4a. Rabbi Ammi in his name, Zevachim 25b; see there. Rabbi Assi (see there); Rav Bibi, Binyamin bar Yefet, Binyamin in his name. Berekhiah; Berekhiah bar Abba bar Kahana in his name. He asked Rav Huna (Yuchasin; I did not find it). Huna bar Chinena before him, Ma'aserot, chapter 5. Hila; Zeira found him; Zekharyah; Ze'ira; Chizkiyah. Chiyya, his teacher (see above). In Chalfai’s name. Chilkiyah, Mani’s father, in his time; Chama and Abba Chanan in his name; Rav Chinena bar Kahana in his name; Chanina bar Ammi. In Chanina’s name, several matters, Megillah 15a; Chanina bar Pappi. Yoshiyah of his generation in his time. Yehudah bar Titus; Yehudah ben Pazi and Yehudah of Sikhnin in his name. He spoke to Yehoshua ben Levi. Rabbi Yochanan, his teacher; Rabbi Yochanan ben Elyakum. Yonah in his name, Kilayim, chapter 9. Yose ben Nehorai ordained him. In Yose ben Zimra’s name. With Yose ben Kisma. In Yannai’s name, Shabbat 141, end of a; see there. Yaakov bar Chama; Yaakov bar Acha; Yaakov bar Adda bar Atalya in his name; Yaakov bar Idi (see there). Yitzchak Tavlaya in his name; Yitzchak Nappacha. He asked Rav Yitzchak bar Avdimi. In Yishmael’s name, Bava Kamma 29b. Rav Kahana; Le'aya and Nasa in his name; Natan bar Abba. In Simai’s name; Simon. Ulla, his student; Ulla Beraya and Ulla son of Yishmael in his name. Pedat, his son; bar Korya. In bar Kappara’s name. Rav, his teacher. Rabbah bar Ofran in his name. R.B.b.T. [רבב״ת; unresolved], see there. He instructed Shuvtay Detzadoki. Shmuel bar Chiyya in his name; Shmuel, his teacher; Shmuel bar Chinena in his name. He comforted Shmuel bar Abba. Shimon bar Abba; Shimon bar Kahana (see there). In Shimon bar Karsena’s name. Shimon ben Elyakum, his student. Shimon bar Meyasha asked him. In Resh Lakish’s name, Ketubbot 49b; in Resh Lakish’s name. Resh Lakish showed him a dinar (Bava Kamma 100a). In Bekhorot 26b, Elazar transmits a separate ruling in Resh Lakish’s name. See there. Rav Sheshet in his name, Yevamot 4a; Zevachim 68b. Tachlifai bar Immi.
